problem.summary: 现有预训练方法（如BERT、GPT）在自然语言生成、翻译和理解任务上的性能存在局限，需要一种更通用、更有效的序列到序列预训练框架。

motivation.summary: 自监督预训练方法在NLP任务中取得显著成功，但现有方法（如掩码语言模型）通常针对特定噪声方案设计，限制了其通用性。BART旨在通过任意噪声函数和重建目标，提供一个更灵活的预训练框架，以统一并超越现有方法。

core_idea.summary: BART是一个去噪自编码器，通过（1）使用任意噪声函数破坏文本，（2）学习模型重建原始文本来预训练序列到序列模型。它使用标准的Transformer编码器-解码器架构，可以泛化BERT（双向编码器）和GPT（自回归解码器）。

method.summary: BART的预训练包括：1）架构：标准Transformer序列到序列模型，编码器双向，解码器自回归；2）噪声变换：实验了多种变换，包括文本填充（Text Infilling）、句子排列（Sentence Permutation）、文档旋转（Document Rotation）等，其中文本填充和句子排列的组合效果最佳；3）预训练目标：优化原始文档的负对数似然；4）微调：可用于序列分类、令牌分类、序列生成和机器翻译等任务。

experiments.summary: 在多个任务上评估：1）判别任务：SQuAD、GLUE等，BART与RoBERTa性能相当；2）生成任务：摘要（CNN/DM、XSum）、对话（ConvAI2）、问答（ELI5），BART取得新SOTA；3）机器翻译：WMT16罗马尼亚语-英语，BART通过仅目标语言预训练提升1.1 BLEU；4）消融实验：比较不同预训练目标，文本填充和句子排列组合表现最佳。

claims.claim: BART在文本生成任务上特别有效，同时在理解任务上也表现良好。
BART在摘要、对话、问答等生成任务上取得新SOTA，ROUGE提升高达6点。
BART通过仅目标语言预训练，为机器翻译提供1.1 BLEU提升。
BART的预训练目标（文本填充和句子排列组合）在多种任务上表现最一致且强劲。
BART的序列到序列预训练可以在不牺牲判别性能的情况下，显著提升生成任务性能。
BART预训练学习了强大的自然语言理解和生成组合能力。

limitations.limitation: 1）机器翻译实验中，BART方法在没有反向翻译数据时效果较差，且容易过拟合；2）预训练数据和计算资源需求较大；3）某些任务（如ELI5）答案仅由问题弱指定，仍具挑战性。

nodes.title: BART整体架构
nodes.label: 架构
nodes.summary: BART采用标准Transformer序列到序列架构，包含双向编码器和自回归解码器。
nodes.description: BART使用标准Transformer编码器-解码器架构，但进行了修改：使用GeLU激活函数，参数从N(0,0.02)初始化。基础模型有6层编码器和解码器，大型模型有12层。解码器每层额外对编码器最终隐藏层进行交叉注意力。与BERT相比，BART没有额外的前馈网络用于词预测，参数多约10%。

nodes.title: 预训练目标
nodes.label: 目标
nodes.summary: BART通过去噪自编码器目标进行预训练：优化原始文档的负对数似然。
nodes.description: BART是去噪自编码器，将损坏文档映射到原始文档。预训练时，优化原始文档的负对数似然（交叉熵损失）。与现有去噪自编码器不同，BART允许应用任意类型的文档损坏。

nodes.title: 噪声变换方法
nodes.label: 噪声
nodes.summary: BART实验了多种文本损坏方法，包括文本填充、句子排列、文档旋转等。
nodes.description: BART支持多种噪声变换：1）文本填充（Text Infilling）：采样文本跨度，长度从泊松分布(λ=3)抽取，每个跨度替换为单个[MASK]令牌；2）句子排列（Sentence Permutation）：基于句号分割文档，随机打乱句子顺序；3）文档旋转（Document Rotation）：随机选择令牌，旋转文档使其以该令牌开始；4）令牌掩码（Token Masking）和令牌删除（Token Deletion）。这些变换可以组合。

nodes.title: 微调方法
nodes.label: 微调
nodes.summary: BART的表示可用于多种下游任务：序列分类、令牌分类、序列生成和机器翻译。
nodes.description: 微调方式：1）序列分类：将相同输入馈入编码器和解码器，使用最终解码器令牌的最终隐藏状态进行分类；2）令牌分类：馈入编码器，解码器用于预测令牌标签；3）序列生成：直接微调用于摘要、问答等生成任务；4）机器翻译：将BART作为预训练解码器，添加新的随机初始化编码器，训练从外语到英语的翻译。

nodes.title: 预训练设置
nodes.label: 设置
nodes.summary: BART使用大规模数据和计算资源进行预训练，采用文本填充和句子排列的组合噪声。
nodes.description: 预训练设置：大型模型有12层编码器和解码器，隐藏大小1024。批次大小8000，训练500000步。使用与GPT-2相同的字节对编码。基于消融实验，使用文本填充和句子排列的组合噪声，掩码30%令牌并排列所有句子。预训练数据为160GB的新闻、书籍、故事和网络文本。

deltas.before: BERT使用掩码语言模型，随机掩码令牌并独立预测，不能直接用于生成。
deltas.after: BART使用去噪自编码器，输入损坏文本，输出重建原始文本，支持任意噪声变换，可直接用于生成。
deltas.why_it_matters: BART统一了双向编码和自回归解码，既能用于理解任务，也能用于生成任务，提供了更通用的预训练框架。

deltas.before: GPT使用自回归语言模型，仅基于左向上下文，不能学习双向交互。
deltas.after: BART的编码器是双向的，解码器是自回归的，允许输入与输出不对齐，支持任意噪声变换。
deltas.why_it_matters: BART结合了双向编码和自回归解码的优势，能够学习更丰富的上下文表示。

deltas.before: 现有去噪自编码器（如SpanBERT）针对特定噪声方案设计，如使用固定长度掩码序列。
deltas.after: BART支持多种噪声变换，包括文本填充（使用泊松分布采样跨度长度，替换为单个掩码令牌）、句子排列等，且这些变换可以组合。
deltas.why_it_matters: BART的噪声方案更灵活，文本填充教会模型预测缺失令牌数量，句子排列教会模型理解文档结构，提升了模型在多种任务上的泛化能力。

deltas.before: 预训练方法在判别任务和生成任务上的性能往往存在权衡。
deltas.after: BART在判别任务（如SQuAD、GLUE）上与RoBERTa性能相当，在生成任务（摘要、对话、问答）上取得新SOTA。
deltas.why_it_matters: BART证明了序列到序列预训练可以在不牺牲判别性能的情况下，显著提升生成任务性能。

deltas.before: 机器翻译中，预训练语言模型在解码器中的应用效果有限。
deltas.after: BART提出将整个预训练模型（编码器和解码器）作为机器翻译的解码器，添加新的随机初始化编码器。
deltas.why_it_matters: 这种方法通过仅目标语言预训练，为机器翻译提供了1.1 BLEU提升，展示了预训练模型在翻译任务中的新应用方式。

glossary.BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training，一种去噪序列到序列预训练方法，通过损坏文本和重建原始文本来预训练模型。
glossary.去噪自编码器: 一种自编码器，通过损坏输入数据并学习重建原始数据来学习表示。
glossary.文本填充: 一种噪声变换，采样文本跨度并替换为单个掩码令牌，跨度长度从泊松分布采样。
glossary.句子排列: 一种噪声变换，将文档分割为句子并随机打乱顺序。
glossary.文档旋转: 一种噪声变换，随机选择令牌并旋转文档使其以该令牌开始。
glossary.序列到序列模型: 一种模型架构，包含编码器和解码器，用于将输入序列映射到输出序列。
glossary.双向编码器: 编码器能够同时利用左向和右向上下文信息。
glossary.自回归解码器: 解码器按顺序生成令牌，每个令牌基于之前生成的令牌。
glossary.标签平滑交叉熵: 一种损失函数，通过平滑标签分布来防止过拟合。

steps.description: 1. 准备预训练数据：收集160GB文本数据，进行字节对编码（与GPT-2相同）。
2. 实现BART架构：基于Transformer序列到序列模型，修改激活函数为GeLU，参数初始化为N(0,0.02)。
3. 实现噪声变换：包括文本填充（泊松分布λ=3）、句子排列、文档旋转等。
4. 预训练：使用文本填充和句子排列的组合噪声，掩码30%令牌，优化负对数似然损失。
5. 微调：根据任务类型（分类、生成、翻译）调整模型结构，使用标签平滑交叉熵损失（平滑参数0.1）。
6. 评估：在相应数据集上评估，使用标准指标（F1、准确率、ROUGE、BLEU等）。

metadata.abstract: We present BART, a denoising autoencoder for pretraining sequence-to-sequence models. BART is trained by (1) corrupting text with an arbitrary noising function, and (2) learning a model to reconstruct the original text. It uses a standard Tranformer-based neural machine translation architecture which, despite its simplicity, can be seen as generalizing BERT (due to the bidirectional encoder), GPT (with the left-to-right decoder), and other recent pretraining schemes. We evaluate a number of noising approaches, finding the best performance by both randomly shuffling the order of sentences and using a novel in-filling scheme, where spans of text are replaced with a single mask token. BART is particularly effective when fine tuned for text generation but also works well for comprehension tasks. It matches the performance of RoBERTa on GLUE and SQuAD, and achieves new state-of-the-art results on a range of abstractive dialogue, question answering, and summarization tasks, with gains of up to 3.5 ROUGE. BART also provides a 1.1 BLEU increase over a back-translation system for machine translation, with only target language pretraining. We also replicate other pretraining schemes within the BART framework, to understand their effect on end-task performance.

2 Model

BART is a denoising autoencoder that maps a corrupted document to the original document it was derived from. It is implemented as a sequence-to-sequence model with a bidirectional encoder over corrupted text and a left-to-right autoregressive decoder. For pre-training,
we optimize the negative log likelihood of the original

2.1 Architecture

BART uses the standard sequence-to-sequence Trans- former architecture from (Vaswani et al., 2017), ex- cept, following GPT, that we modify ReLU activa- tion functions to GeLUs (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) and initialise parameters from N (0, 0.02). For our base model, we use 6 layers in the encoder and de-
coder, and for our large model we use 12 layers in

each. The architecture is closely related to that used in BERT, with the following differences: (1) each layer of the decoder additionally performs cross-attention over the ﬁnal hidden layer of the encoder (as in the trans- former sequence-to-sequence model); and (2) BERT uses an additional feed-forward network before word- prediction, which BART does not. In total, BART con- tains roughly 10% more parameters than the equiva- lently sized BERT model.
2.2 Pre-training BART

BART is trained by corrupting documents and then op- timizing a reconstruction loss—the cross-entropy be- tween the decoder’s output and the original document. Unlike existing denoising autoencoders, which are tai- lored to speciﬁc noising schemes, BART allows us to apply any type of document corruption. In the extreme case, where all information about the source is lost, BART is equivalent to a language model. We experiment with several previously proposed and novel transformations, but we believe there is a sig- niﬁcant potential for development of other new alter- natives. 8 Conclusions
We introduced BART, a pre-training approach that learns to map corrupted documents to the original. BART achieves similar performance to RoBERTa on
discriminative tasks, while achieving new state-of-the-

2 Model

BART is a denoising autoencoder that maps a corrupted document to the original document it was derived from. It is implemented as a sequence-to-sequence model with a bidirectional encoder over corrupted text and a left-to-right autoregressive decoder. For pre-training,
we optimize the negative log likelihood of the original
document.
2.1 Architecture

BART uses the standard sequence-to-sequence Trans- former architecture from (Vaswani et al., 2017), ex- cept, following GPT, that we modify ReLU activa- tion functions to GeLUs (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) and initialise parameters from N (0, 0.02). For our base model, we use 6 layers in the encoder and de-
coder, and for our large model we use 12 layers in

each. The architecture is closely related to that used in BERT, with the following differences: (1) each layer of the decoder additionally performs cross-attention over the ﬁnal hidden layer of the encoder (as in the trans- former sequence-to-sequence model); and (2) BERT uses an additional feed-forward network before word- prediction, which BART does not. In total, BART con- tains roughly 10% more parameters than the equiva- lently sized BERT model.
2.2 Pre-training BART

BART is trained by corrupting documents and then op- timizing a reconstruction loss—the cross-entropy be- tween the decoder’s output and the original document. Unlike existing denoising autoencoders, which are tai- lored to speciﬁc noising schemes, BART allows us to apply any type of document corruption. In the extreme case, where all information about the source is lost, BART is equivalent to a language model. We experiment with several previously proposed and novel transformations, but we believe there is a sig- niﬁcant potential for development of other new alter- natives. The transformations we used are summarized below, and examples are shown in Figure 2. Token Masking Following BERT (Devlin et al., 2019), random tokens are sampled and replaced with [MASK] elements. 3 Fine-tuning BART

The representations produced by BART can be used in several ways for downstream applications. 3.1 Sequence Classiﬁcation Tasks For sequence classiﬁcation tasks, the same input is fed into the encoder and decoder, and the ﬁnal hidden state of the ﬁnal decoder token is fed into new multi-class linear classiﬁer. This approach is related to the CLS token in BERT; however we add the additional token to the end so that representation for the token in the decoder can attend to decoder states from the complete input (Figure 3a). 3.2 Token Classiﬁcation Tasks For token classiﬁcation tasks, such as answer endpoint classiﬁcation for SQuAD, we feed the complete doc- ument into the encoder and decoder, and use the top hidden state of the decoder as a representation for each word. This representation is used to classify the token.
3.3 Sequence Generation Tasks

Because BART has an autoregressive decoder, it can be directly ﬁne tuned for sequence generation tasks such as abstractive question answering and summarization. In both of these tasks, information is copied from the input but manipulated, which is closely related to the denoising pre-training objective. Here, the encoder in- put is the input sequence, and the decoder generates outputs autoregressively.
3.4 Machine Translation

We also explore using BART to improve machine trans- lation decoders for translating into English. Previous work Edunov et al. (2019) has shown that models can be improved by incorporating pre-trained encoders, but gains from using pre-trained language models in de- coders have been limited. We show that it is possible to use the entire BART model (both encoder and de- coder) as a single pretrained decoder for machine trans- lation, by adding a new set of encoder parameters that are learned from bitext (see Figure 3b). More precisely, we replace BART’s encoder embed- ding layer with a new randomly initialized encoder. The model is trained end-to-end, which trains the new encoder to map foreign words into an input that BART can de-noise to English. The new encoder can use a separate vocabulary from the original BART model. 7 Related Work

Early methods for pretraining were based on language models. GPT (Radford et al., 2018) only models left- ward context, which is problematic for some tasks. ELMo (Peters et al., 2018) concatenates left-only and right-only representations, but does not pre-train inter- actions between these features. Radford et al. (2019)
demonstrated that very large language models can act

as unsupervised multitask models. BERT (Devlin et al., 2019) introduced masked lan- guage modelling, which allows pre-training to learn in- teractions between left and right context words. Re- cent work has shown that very strong performance can be achieved by training for longer (Liu et al., 2019), by tying parameters across layers (Lan et al., 2019), and by masking spans instead of words (Joshi et al., 2019). Predictions are not made auto-regressively, re- ducing the effectiveness of BERT for generation tasks. UniLM (Dong et al., 2019) ﬁne-tunes BERT with an ensemble of masks, some of which allow only leftward context. Like BART, this allows UniLM to be used for
both generative and discriminative tasks. A difference

is that UniLM predictions are conditionally indepen- dent, whereas BART’s are autoregressive. BART re- duces the mismatch between pre-training and genera- tion tasks, because the decoder is always trained on un- corrupted context. MASS (Song et al., 2019) is perhaps the most similar model to BART. An input sequence where a contiguous span of tokens is masked is mapped to a sequence con- sisting of the missing tokens. 8 Conclusions
We introduced BART, a pre-training approach that learns to map corrupted documents to the original. BART achieves similar performance to RoBERTa on
discriminative tasks, while achieving new state-of-the-
art results on a number of text generation tasks. Fu- ture work should explore new methods for corrupting documents for pre-training, perhaps tailoring them to speciﬁc end tasks.
